BUILDING THE NETWORK | G4-G6 | 2019-2022
Capital commitments and operating design
|
+-- Original design: software over partner capacity
|   [S] $1B five-year envelope was mostly variable fulfillment cost.
|   [S] Ottawa R&D site; provision for two possible test warehouses.
|   [S] Through 2021: $117M cash operating losses plus small capex.
|   [I] That net funding measure is not gross fulfillment spend.
|
+-- More direct operation announced in February 2022
|   [S] Self-operated LEASED hubs plus partner warehouses.
|   [S] $1B capex for 2023-24; scale targeted late 2023 into 2024.
|   [S] Same call: $2B through 2024, including $1.4B capex.
|   [I] Different capex windows are not reconciled in the excerpts.
|
+-- Deliverr: purchase accounting, not capex
|   [R] $1,961.864M cash + $9.774M shares = $1,971.638M price.
|   [R] Another $293.688M in awards treated as compensation.
|   [R] Goodwill: $1,437.664M of purchase price.
|   [I] Low capex therefore does not mean a low-cost experiment.
|
+-- Operating reality and retrenchment
|   [S] Q3 2022: Atlanta hub functioning; local fulfillment via 3PLs.
|   [S] Q4 2022: defer capex ramp until Deliverr integration.
|   [S] 2023 logistics capex incurred in first two quarters: $33M.
|   [I] $33M / $1B = 3.3%; truncated period versus two-year PLAN.
|   [X] Small capex proves that no self-operated facilities existed.
|
Evidence: B1-B5; operating versus owning is a material distinction.
